abstract: Maintains acoustic grid clearances, sonar coverage benchmarks, and subsea positioning authorizations
system_message:
You are Chief Hydrographic Surveyor (CHS). As Chief Hydrographic Surveyor (CHS), you maintain official records concerning acoustic grid clearances, sonar coverage benchmarks, and subsea positioning authorizations across subsea survey operations, in addition to overseeing sound velocity profiler calibration intervals.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Sound velocity profiling（SOUND）
information_points.content:
CHS-SOUND-JYZ：The sound velocity profile probe calibration interval for the CTD and velocimeter arrays assigned to the Autonomous benthic crawler transect is 90 d.
CHS-SOUND-2IH：For the Towed synthetic aperture sonar run, the sound velocity profile probe calibration interval for the assigned sensor arrays stands at 60 d.
CHS-SOUND-5OR：The Dual-workclass ROV trench sweep reflects a sound velocity profile probe calibration interval of 30 d for its assigned mobilization vessel profiling equipment.

information_points.title: Maintains acoustic grid clearances, sonar coverage benchmarks, and subsea positioning authorizations（ACOUST）
information_points.content:
CHS-ACOUST-1WV：The Towed synthetic aperture sonar run holds acoustic survey grid authorization for the corridor sector intersecting the damaged HVDC trench and deep-tow acoustic transponder deployment authorization for the seabed beacon baseline array, with its flight plan showing a side-scan sonar seabed coverage of 80% across the 12 square kilometers target search polygon.
CHS-ACOUST-IBC：For the Autonomous benthic crawler transect, acoustic survey grid authorization is confirmed across the corridor sector intersecting the damaged HVDC trench, and deep-tow acoustic transponder deployment authorization is granted for the seabed beacon baseline array. Its mission flight plan establishes a side-scan sonar seabed coverage of 85% over the 12 square kilometers target fault search polygon.
CHS-ACOUST-I3G：For the Dual-workclass ROV trench sweep, acoustic survey grid authorization is valid within the corridor sector intersecting the damaged HVDC trench, deep-tow acoustic transponder deployment authorization is secured for the seabed beacon baseline array, and side-scan sonar seabed coverage reaches 95% over the 12 square kilometers target fault search polygon.
